name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index eased to 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 in October, down 1.6 points (1.2%) from a revised September level, with cereals 4.5% lower and sugar up 6.6% to its highest since December 2024 (FAO, 6 Nov). The index is below the 135 Alert line but 5.9% above a year earlier, which meets the Watch line.
for_you: Food-importing countries and low-income households are most exposed. Sugar and vegetable oils were the upward pressures in October, while cereals eased.
rubric_hit: FFPI 133.9 inside the 120–135 Watch band; y/y +5.9% above the +5% Watch line
why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
